title: DevOps, Cloud-Native CI/CD & DORA Delivery Excellence
summary: Build cloud-native CI/CD pipelines, execute zero-downtime rolling updates and rollbacks, and optimize Elite DORA engineering metrics.
learningObjectives: Execute controlled zero-downtime rolling image updates and instant rollbacks on Kubernetes Deployments.
Provision ephemeral Kubernetes-native CI runner workloads.
Measure and optimize the four DORA metrics (Deployment Frequency, Lead Time, Change Failure Rate, MTTR).

curriculumModules.title: Immutable Artifact Promotion & Zero-Downtime Rolling Updates
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Build container images once at commit SHA, scan and sign them, and promote the identical digest across Dev -> Staging -> Production using `RollingUpdate` maxSurge/maxUnavailable.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Configure `maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 25%` with a `readinessProbe` so old pods are never terminated until new pods pass health checks.

curriculumModules.title: DORA Metrics & Ephemeral Kubernetes CI Runners
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Elite engineering teams measure Lead Time for Changes, Deployment Frequency, Change Failure Rate, and Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) using ephemeral Kubernetes runner pods.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Run self-hosted GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC) or Tekton Pipelines in an isolated namespace with rootless buildkit builds.

labs.title: Zero-Downtime Rolling Release & Artifact Verification
labs.scenario: Promote release `ghcr.io/kubelabs/frontend:v2.5.0` to the `web-frontend` deployment in `production` and verify its cryptographic signature.
labs.productionContext: Every production deployment should verify image signatures (`cosign`) and confirm rollout completion across all replicas.
objectives: Verify the artifact signature using `cosign verify`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-frontend
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-frontend
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-frontend
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: ghcr.io/kubelabs/frontend:v2.5.0

steps.title: Verify OCI Image Signature
steps.instruction: Run `cosign verify ghcr.io/kubelabs/frontend:v2.5.0` to verify SLSA provenance.

steps.title: Promote Image to Production Deployment
steps.commandHint: kubectl set image deployment/web-frontend web=ghcr.io/kubelabs/frontend:v2.5.0 -n production

validationRules.name: web-frontend
validationRules.remediation: Run `kubectl set image deployment/web-frontend web=ghcr.io/kubelabs/frontend:v2.5.0 -n production`.

solutionCommands: kubectl set image deployment/web-frontend web=ghcr.io/kubelabs/frontend:v2.5.0 -n production

labs.title: Emergency Rollback of Defective Production Deployment
labs.scenario: A defective release (`ghcr.io/kubelabs/cart:v3.0-broken`) was pushed to `cart-service` in `production`. Execute an immediate rollback to restore service health.
labs.productionContext: Minimizing Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) requires immediate rollback via `kubectl rollout undo` when a bad release slips into production.
objectives: Roll back `deployment/cart-service` in `production` using `kubectl rollout undo`
Verify all `cart-service` pods return to `Running` state
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cart-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cart-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cart-service
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: cart
          image: ghcr.io/kubelabs/cart:v3.0-stable

steps.title: Observe Broken Rollout
steps.instruction: Run `kubectl get pods -n production` to see `cart-service` failing.

validationRules.description: Deployment production/cart-service rolled back to stable image
validationRules.name: cart-service
cart-service
validationRules.remediation: Confirm pods are Running after rollback.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Run `kubectl rollout undo deployment/cart-service -n production` and verify with `kubectl get pods -n production`.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which four metrics constitute the standard DORA software delivery performance metrics?
options: Lines of Code, Story Points, Sprint Velocity, Bug Count
Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate, Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
CPU Usage, Memory Usage, Disk IOPS, Network Bandwidth
Number of Microservices, Number of Clusters, Number of Engineers, Cloud Spend
assessmentQuestions.explanation: DORA research established Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate, and Time to Restore Service (MTTR) as the four key indicators of software delivery performance.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which RollingUpdate settings ensure zero capacity loss during a deployment upgrade?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Setting `maxUnavailable: 0` with positive `maxSurge` guarantees old pods remain serving traffic until newly surged pods pass their `readinessProbe`.
